newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian stocks end sleepy session firmer.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian stocks end sleepy session firmer.

text.p: SPI Futures cl 2334 +9 US 30yr 6.70 +0.04
10yrbond futs 92.410 -0.030 Gold NY 369.30 Lon fix 368.00
*Stocks ended a quiet session firmer after the Dow managed to bounce back again on Wednesday. Volume 338.9 million, value A$764.2 million, 1,004 stocks traded, 305 steady, 378 up, 321 down.
Australian shares ended a quiet session near its highs on Thursday following a stronger Dow from the open while firmer base metals prices underpinned the resource sector.
The All Ordinaries index closed eight points higher at 2,331.7, close to its intra-session high of 2,332.8.
December share price index futures ended nine points firmer at 2,334 and at a 3.3 point premium to the underlying index.
Turnover picked up late in the day as December option expiries started to be put through the market. Dealers said the bulk of expiries would be reflected in Friday's turnover.
"The market followed through this afternoon and it was a reasonably impressive performance given the time of the year," said Jim Tredenick, senior dealer at Brisbane broker, Nevitts.
Tredenick said investors were happy to pick up bluechip resource and industrial issues on the day and there was also good demand for the more prospective junior gold miners.
"There has been a lot of interest in the Gawler Craton region of South Australia and investors were looking for value stocks with interests in this area today," Tredenick said.
Resources faired better than industrials with bellwether resource group CRA having a better session on Thursday.

Market focus was on regional banks Advance and St George as investors weighed up the possibility that National Australia Bank may try to block the planned merger of the two regionals when Advance shareholders meet to approve the merger on Monday.
Advance stock was adversely affected by the speculation while St George shares rose.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures and options trade was moderate with options business most active in major resource issues as investors rolled December contracts to later months.
Total options traded 60,476 (36,527)
Turnover in December SPI contracts totalled 5,459 (6,272)
In other local markets, Australian bonds succumbed to their slowest trading session for some weeks as the market wound down for the year-end holidays.
The yield on 10 year T-bonds closed at 7.48 percent, up 0.05 percentage points from Wednesday's close.

The Australian dollar spent most of the day snaking around the US$0.7910 support level before a late rise saw it finish an uneventful day around the middle of the US$0.7910/50 range it has spent most of the past week in.
At 5.15 p.m. (0615 GMT) the unit was trading at US$0.7918/23, down slightly on Wednesday's US$0.7925/30 close.

Regional bank shares hit by newspaper report highlighting speculation that National Australia Bank may attempt to thwart Advance's planned merger with St George at a shareholders meeting on Monday.
Gawler Craton explorer surged after good drilling results.
Major miners ended firmer after base metals prices strengthened on Wednesday.
